questions.q: Which is a real topic sentence: 'I am going to write about my school' or 'My school is the noisiest, friendliest building I know'?
questions.a: The second — it states an idea about the school; the first announces the writing instead of doing it. A wrong answer shows the student doesn't see announcing as a dodge.

questions.q: Find the weed: 'My garden has many flowers. Roses are red and smell sweet. My uncle lives in Jaipur. The marigolds bloom in winter.'
questions.a: 'My uncle lives in Jaipur' — off-topic. A wrong answer keeping it reveals the student grades paragraphs by sentence count, not by idea-unity.

questions.q: Write the closing line for a paragraph about your pet's funny habits.
questions.a: Any line that lands on the pet — e.g., 'With a tail that never stops wagging, she makes every day a little circus.' A wrong answer 'And that's all about my pet' shows the announcing-error at the closing end.

questions.q: A paragraph is one idea in a wrapper: a topic sentence that names the idea, three or four ______ sentences that feed it, and a closing sentence that ties it off.
Fill in the blank: A paragraph is one idea in a wrapper: a topic sentence that names the idea, three or four ______ sentences that feed it, and a closing sentence that ties it off.

Fill in the blank: Build one aloud — topic 'My school library': topic ______ ('Our school library is my favourite place'), supports (the books, the silence, the librarian), closer ('It is where I travel without moving').
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student writes a 5-6 sentence paragraph with a clear topic sentence, on-topic supports, and a closing line; and can name which sentence in a given paragraph wanders off-topic.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Build one aloud — topic 'My school library': topic sentence ('Our school library is my ______ place'), supports (the books, the silence, the librarian), closer ('It is where I travel without moving').
